open_points.subject: store.page_records pagination with mutable filters
open_points.text: “The continuation token is the store position of the last item returned; the next page starts below it” and “a record whose filtered field (a status) changes between pages leaves or enters the pages still to come”
open_points.question: If a record above the continuation position did not match earlier but changes to match before the next page, must it appear despite being above the cursor, or are filter changes considered only for records below the cursor?
options: Only records below the cursor are reconsidered using their current field values
Newly matching records above the cursor are also returned
Filter membership is snapshotted on the first page
open_points.default_guess: Only records below the cursor are reconsidered using their current field values

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list after a failed re-read
open_points.text: “Re-read when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read” and “a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes”
open_points.question: After a failed re-read, must every later request retry parsing until one succeeds, including when the restored file has exactly the same bytes as the last successfully loaded file?
options: Retry on every request while no valid token list exists
Retry only when the bytes differ from the last successful digest or the file is unreadable
open_points.default_guess: Retry on every request while no valid token list exists

open_points.subject: runs.read_run inspection result
open_points.text: “A run's answer, wherever an operation returns one, holds: `run_id`, the flow version, status, starter and times, outputs produced, waiting points…”
open_points.question: How can inspection return the Run facts that M19 says the owner and agents read but this answer omits: inputs, pinned implementations, resumptions and `cancelled_by`?
options: Include those M19 facts in every run answer
Expose them only through a separate raw-run inspection operation
Intentionally make those stored facts unavailable through the surface
open_points.default_guess: Include those M19 facts in every run answer

open_points.subject: historical Activation and FlowActivation inspection
open_points.text: “activations are read through `get_slot`, flow activations through `get_flow`” while `functions.read_slot` returns only “its current activation” and `flows.active_flow_version` returns only “its active flow version and FlowActivation”
open_points.question: How is a caller to read a non-current Activation or FlowActivation, including one named by store position as an EffectAttempt's authority?
options: Add lookup or listing by activation store position
Historical activations are intentionally opaque and only their positions are returned

open_points.subject: agent-visible failure_detail masking
open_points.question: What does `length` measure, and is it the length of the retained bounded detail or of the original unbounded detail?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the retained bounded detail
Unicode code-point length of the retained bounded detail
open_points.default_guess: UTF-8 byte length of the retained bounded detail

open_points.subject: store.remove_run_spool I/O failure
open_points.text: State 3 says “every failure it answers `internal_error` — a store failure … is answered first, and then `surface.serve_kernel` ends the process”, while State 5 says spool removal “never fails a request” and `store.remove_run_spool` returns “`internal_error` on an I/O failure; its caller does not fail the request”
open_points.question: When spool removal fails after the run or release record is committed, what response is returned and does the kernel stop afterward?
options: Return the successful run response and continue serving, retrying removal at a later start
Return the successful run response and then stop the process
Return `internal_error` and then stop the process
open_points.default_guess: Return the successful run response and continue serving, retrying removal at a later start
